newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's Lafarge to invest $21.7 mln in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's Lafarge to invest $21.7 mln in 1997/98.

text.p: Morocco's Lafarge Ciments holding said on Friday it will invest 200 million dirhams ($21.7 million) to upgrade the group's infrastructure and boost its cement output.

In a news conference at the Lafarge Ciments headquarters, managing director Alain lemeure announced the group's consolidated pre-tax profits of 217 million dirhams ($23.5 million) in 1996, or an increase of 38 percent over the previous year.
"We plan to invest up to 200 million dirhams in a two-year plan starting from 1997 to upgrade the Lafarge Ciments infrastructure and develop its activities," Lemeure told reporters.
The group registered a turnover of 1.4 billion dirhams in 1996, slightly up from 1.3 billion dirhams in 1995, Lemeure said.
"The improvement of 1996 pre-tax result is due to the management efforts and synergies of the group active units," Alain Lemeure, the group's managing director said.
The group, which holds 42 percent of cement market share, showed a net profit of 152 million dirhams ($16.5 million) in 1996 from 135 million dirhams ($14.6 million) in 1995.
It will distribute a total dividend of 85.7 million dirhams on the basis of 18 dirhams per share, officials said.
He estimated at 646 million dirhams the group's total debt which he said will be reimbursed by the year 2000.
"We noticed that the reduction by 50 percent of our financial costs due to interest rates discount and cutting down of debt were behind this positive result," Lemeure said.

Holding Lafarge Ciment is made up of Lafarge Ciment, which includes cement firms Cinouca and Cadem since January 1996, has interests in two cement firms in the northern cities of Tangier and Tetuan, the statement said.
Lafarge Ciments sold 2.67 million tonnes of cement products mainly on the domestic market in 1996 against 2.63 million tonnes in 1995, Lemeure added.
French group Lafarge Coppee together with Morocco's conglomerate Societe Nationale d'Investissement own 50 percent of Lafarge Maroc.
One of the 47 stocks listed on the Casablanca stock exchange, it was last traded at 1,360 dirhams.
